caption: The drawing features a single symmetrical object resembling a classical pedestal bowl or chalice, rendered in graphite or pencil on a light beige, slightly textured paper. The bowl has a wide, shallow upper section, a pronounced, rounded lip, and a slightly inward-curving body that transitions into a narrower, concave stem. This stem sits atop a broad, rounded base that provides stability. The form is shaded to indicate curvature and depth, suggesting three-dimensionality. The main object is enclosed within a square frame centered on the page. Below the image, a scale bar is marked, and the name “MEYERS” is written to the lower left of the square. Additionally, in the bottom right corner, there is a smaller inset drawing, also in pencil, depicting the same object in reduced size. Handwritten measurement annotations are visible next to the smaller drawing, indicating dimensions. The composition uses only shades of grey and the off-white tone of the paper, with all elements precisely aligned and neatly arranged on the page.
title: Pewter Bowl
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
